analysis.title: Balancing Act Monthly Insights: Global Multi-Asset (October 2026)
key_insights: Global equities fell in September as higher bond yields, higher oil prices and a stronger USD weighed on markets. MSCI ACWI returned -1.3% in USD terms. AI-linked US semiconductors and hyperscalers rose but did not offset broader weakness.
The Fed raised its benchmark rate by 25 bps to 3.75-4% mid-September, its first hike since July 2023. Updated projections point to the possibility of another hike before year-end.

Global government bonds sold off and long-dated yields reached multi-decade highs. The 2-year and 10-year UST yields ended September at 4.89% and 5.29%, up 55 bps and 54 bps from end-August. The front end sold off slightly more after a stronger-than-expected August core CPI.

Gold fell 6.3% in September on higher yields and dollar strength. WTI rose 5.4% on US-Iran tensions, Strait of Hormuz and Saudi bypass route supply concerns, and attacks on regional energy infrastructure. Global REITs (FTSE NAREIT Global Real Estate) fell 5.4%.

Team keeps marginal overweights in both growth and defensive scores. Positive on risk assets but cautious on equity volatility from the US-Iran conflict, inflation pressure and the early-November US midterm elections.

Overweight DM equities, with US earnings growth backed by AI capex expected to carry into the next reporting season. Overweight EM equities, with Taiwan favoured on AI buildout, robust earnings and cheaper valuations versus developed markets. Neutral on commodity-linked equities. Underweight REITs and infrastructure.
Overweight UK equities for a value tilt (financials, materials, energy), low-beta staples and healthcare, and high dividend yields.

Moved DM sovereigns back to overweight after the September bond sell-off. Remains underweight IG and HY credit because spreads sit at historical lows, inflation is rising and central banks are tightening.

Expects the Fed policy rate to rise toward 5% and the 10-year UST to trade in a 5.0-5.5% range. Moved from underweight to marginal overweight US duration and would add more if yields approach 5.5%. Raised the dollar score back to overweight on rate differentials and hawkish Fed.

Energy: US retail diesel is at record highs, with refined products tighter than crude. The conflict expanded into the Red Sea after the collapse of the US-Iran memorandum of understanding. Gulf exports are recovering through protected tanker movements and ship-to-ship transfers, but insurance, freight and security costs keep delivered prices high.

Non-conflict supply is responding (US drilling, Canada, Brazil, Venezuela exports to US and India). A US-Iran settlement could quickly return the oil market to surplus and create significant downside risk for energy. The team expects prices to stay high near term, with supply adaptation limiting further increases.

Yen: the BOJ is hiking, but the team argues the pace of Japanese rate convergence with other central banks matters more than direction. The yen keeps its funding-currency role at the margin because the Swiss franc, Singapore dollar and Chinese yuan each have drawbacks as substitutes.

vol_and_positioning: The team is cautious about equity market volatility from the US-Iran conflict, inflation pressure and the US midterm elections.
Credit spreads sit at historical lows, offering little buffer against a bond sell-off. The team expects widening on negative news and keeps credit exposure short.
The yen has been a funding currency with low borrowing costs and relatively low volatility, but sharp appreciation episodes and intervention concerns have periodically disrupted carry positions.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict continues after the collapse of the memorandum of understanding and its expansion into the Red Sea
Supply disruption concerns around the Strait of Hormuz and the Saudi bypass route, with renewed attacks on regional energy infrastructure
Attacks on energy infrastructure in the Middle East and Russia have reduced effective refining capacity
China has restricted refined product exports and Indian refiners are struggling to secure feedstock
Trump coordinated strategic inventory releases with G7 partners, urged Ukraine to halt attacks on Russian refineries and negotiated a diesel deal with Moscow

tension_points.theme: US equities versus inflation and Fed hikes
tension_points.bull_case: Strong earnings growth, supported by AI capex, lets investors look past high energy prices and a hawkish Fed, and valuations are not extended.
tension_points.bear_case: Stronger data and stickier inflation could prompt a series of Fed hikes during a mid-cycle expansion, and the US-Iran conflict has no decisive end in sight.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A series of Fed rate hikes to adjust the inflation trajectory, or a prolonged conflict or renewed damage to key chokepoints keeping commodity prices higher for longer.

tension_points.bull_case: Prolonged conflict or chokepoint damage keeps crude and diesel elevated near term.
tension_points.bear_case: A US-Iran political settlement could quickly return the market to a surplus, with significant downside for the energy complex, and supply chains are adapting.

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong economic activity and a resilient labour market may keep inflation as the Fed's main focus, so further tightening is expected.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect further policy tightening, with the policy rate rising toward 5%

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong earnings growth backed by steady AI capex lets US equities overlook energy and inflation headwinds.
theme_stances.evidence: US equities may overlook these headwinds given the strength of the earnings outlook

theme_stances.key_argument: Prices stay high near term, but supply adaptation should limit further increases and a settlement could return the market to surplus.
theme_stances.evidence: prices will remain high in the near term

theme_stances.key_argument: The yen may become less attractive as a funding currency at the margin without losing its structural role, because no obvious successor exists.
theme_stances.evidence: there is currently no obvious successor
